messages:
Maria L: quick heads-up — noticed a regression in private tenants when we fallback to model variants across regions. some onprem customers have very tight egress allowlists and the current fallback can route them to EU models even though their allowlist only permits US egress.
Jonathan K: can you paste the example tenant id and the routing decision log?
Maria L: tenant=t-82734. log snippet: `route_decision: fallback -> model=falcon-small-v2, region=eu-west-1, reason=capacity_pressure, tenant_allowed_regions=[us-east-1]` — so we violated the tenant constraint earlier in the pipeline.
Kai W: hmm that implies the routing layer that chooses fallback variants doesn't consult the tenant-level egress policy, or we lose the constraint when we map model->region.
Rachel S: security: this is urgent. Private control plane must never route outside allowed regions. We need an explicit invariant: fallback_region ∈ tenant_allowed_regions. If not, fallback must fail open to onprem-only variant or return 503 with clear error.
Samir P: from a product POV we want graceful degradation, not hard failures for all customers. Can we offer a per-tenant opt-in to cross-region fallback? for some customers they accept it if they sign off. Console should show a warning and explicit consent.
Jonathan K: technically we have three places to handle this: 1) routing decision engine, 2) model placement mapping (model->region candidates), 3) control-plane enforcement for onprem. I think we should enforce in the routing decision engine as a hard filter, and expose an override flag for consented tenants.
Kai W: agree. implementation idea: add `egress_constraints` into the routing context and filter candidate regions early. pseudocode: ```c
candidates = rank_models(query)
candidates = filter(candidates, candidate.region in ctx.egress_constraints.allowed_regions)
if candidates.empty and ctx.tenant_consent.cross_region_fallback:
  candidates = rank_models(query) // re-evaluate with consent
else if candidates.empty:
  return error(LOCKED_EGRESS, "no eligible fallback within allowed regions")
```
Rachel S: also need telemetry and audit: log both the filtered candidates and the final decision, mark when consent was used. we must retain these logs for compliance (30d min).
Samir P: console UX: show a per-model badge like "cross-region fallback: blocked" and expose a single-click consent toggle that documents the trade-offs and writes a signed consent record.
Maria L: one more edge: some tenants have allowed_regions but also a private network egress-check that only allows specific IP ranges. Even if region matches, the specific endpoint might not. we should include `egress_endpoints` in the constraints.
Kai W: good call. we'll add `allowed_endpoints` to the context and check endpoint reachability at deploy-time (probe) and at runtime as best-effort.
Jonathan K: for rollout: propose a staged deploy — start with telemetry-only mode that filters and logs but still allows fallback (no tenant impact) for 48h; then enforce blocking + console opt-in. ops-bot, schedule deploy windows?
ops-bot: deploy window booked: canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC, ramp over 2h -> prod 03:00+48h if no regressions. :calendar:
deploy-bot: patch branch `routing/egress-filter-ctx` built and queued for canary. CI green.
Rachel S: plus, add an alert if we see >1% private requests hit LOCKED_EGRESS in canary so we can revert quickly.
Samir P: ok product will prepare the consent modal and audit message. engineers — who owns the routing and console bits?
Kai W: routing: eng-runtime. console + consent store: eng-platform.
Maria L: perfect. next steps: (1) add egress constraints to routing context PR by EOD (Kai), (2) telemetry-only canary tomorrow (Jonathan), (3) consent modal spec (Samir) by EOD, (4) audit retention + alert (Rachel). I'll follow up in a short doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Jonathan K: adding a quick test matrix in the ticket: private tenant (allowed_regions=[us-east-1]) + capacity pressure -> expect LOCKED_EGRESS unless consent. Also tests for allowed_endpoints mismatch. I'll link tests in the PR.
Maria L: linking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321
Samir P: pinging @Rachel S for compliance blurb for the modal copy, thanks.
Rachel S: will drop a short blurb in the ticket by EOD.
Maria L: end.
